data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Struggles After OpenAI Revenue Disclosure
data.description:
The stock of chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) is down 1% a day after artificial intelligence (AI) startup OpenAI disclosed revised revenue figures that have rattled investors. The decline on Oct. 9 comes after NVDA stock dropped 3% in the previous trading session on news of OpenAI's sales.

Stocks of companies tied to the artificial intelligence (A.I.) buildout fell after OpenAI announced a revised revenue figure that fell short of Wall Street's expectations. Beyond Nvidia, shares of Oracle (ORCL), CoreWeave (CRWV), and others, fell after the market learned more details about OpenAI's sales data.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Top Five Biggest Video Game Stock Stories This Week, 10/9/26
data.description:
The video game industry saw big announcements this week. Console sales fell as prices rose, while Xbox hinted at new hardware plans. Nintendo also set up a busy holiday season, and Sony explored new ways to engage stream viewers. Meanwhile, Cyberpunk 2077 is heading to the big screen.

1. Game Hardware Sales Hit a 13-Year Low

A global shortage of memory and storage parts has pushed console prices higher. Sony (SONY), Microsoft (MSFT), and Nintendo (NTDOY) have all raised prices. New data from Circana shows that U.S. game hardware sales fell 15% year over year in August. Sales hit their lowest level since 2013, as higher prices may be keeping some buyers away from new systems.

2. Xbox Hints at a New Handheld

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has fueled talk of a new Xbox handheld. The device may be part of the next-gen hardware line known as Project Helix. This also isn't the first time reports of an Xbox handheld have spread online. The hints come as Sony faces questions about its own plans for a handheld system. Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has warned that Sony has often struggled to market a home console and a handheld at the same time.

3. Nintendo Plans a Big Zelda Holiday Push

Nintendo is lining up four major releases in a tight 14-day span to mark the Zelda series' 40th anniversary. The plan is to release new games and hardware during the holiday season. The schedule is said to end with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, which is set to launch worldwide on November 5, 2026.

4. Sony Patent Lets Stream Viewers Join the Game

Sony has filed a patent for tech that could let viewers affect a streamer's gameplay. The system could give viewers control of a shared on-screen cursor or let them send signals based on their reactions. These tools could help fans guide a player—or make the game harder. The idea could add a new layer of audience input to live game streams.

5. Cyberpunk 2077 Is Getting a Live-Action Film

CD Projekt Red (OTGLF) is teaming up with Skydance (SKYD)'s Paramount Pictures to co-produce a live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film. The project will bring the game world to the big screen. It adds to the growing link between video games and film, as game-based stories reach fans across more forms of media.

data.title: 'It's Far From Bleak,' Says Top Investor About Oracle Stock
data.description:
Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) stock is climbing around 5% on Friday, recovering from Thursday's selloff as investors reassess the financial strength of one of its largest customers, OpenAI. The ChatGPT developer has signed a $300 billion cloud computing agreement with Oracle, making its ability to finance future commitments particularly important to the software giant's outlook.

Thursday's losses followed a Financial Times report putting OpenAI's annualized revenue at roughly $50 billion in late September, below earlier estimates of nearly $70 billion, with differences in revenue accounting contributing to the discrepancy. However, Bloomberg subsequently reported that the ChatGPT developer expects its annualized revenue to reach or exceed $70 billion by year-end, helping ease concerns about its ability to meet its extensive infrastructure commitments.

Yet, while Oracle's reliance on OpenAI and mounting debt have worried investors, one top investor believes the market may be overlooking several reasons for optimism.

Promotion

Bay Area Ideas, who ranks among the top 4% of stock experts on TipRanks, assigns a Buy rating to Oracle stock despite its nearly 27% loss this year, arguing that the company's expanding AI operations offer investors reasons for optimism. (To watch Bay Area Ideas' track record, click here)

One reason for his confidence is Oracle's latest quarterly performance, which showed revenue climbing 30% year-over-year to $19.3 billion in fiscal Q1 2027. That marked an acceleration from 21% growth in the preceding quarter, while cloud infrastructure sales surged 121%, compared with 93% previously.

The investor also points to Oracle's $664 billion in remaining performance obligations (RPO), representing contracted revenue that has yet to be recognized. Those commitments increased by $209 billion from a year earlier, offering greater visibility into potential future revenue, although their realization depends on customers fulfilling their contracts.

However, Oracle's aggressive infrastructure spending has raised legitimate concerns about its financial health, particularly after negative free cash flow reached $5 billion during the quarter.

"Risks are real, but I believe there is a chance that investors may have become overly fearful of the situation," Bay Area Ideas opined.

His assessment takes into account Oracle's ability to access financing beyond traditional borrowing, including a $20 billion equity offering during the first quarter. Although additional stock issuance could dilute existing investors, such alternatives provide flexibility as infrastructure construction continues.

Meanwhile, the company's liquidity ratios remain acceptable in Bay Area's assessment, reducing the likelihood of immediate financial difficulties despite elevated leverage. The investor also believes contractual profitability and expanding international demand could support Oracle's longer-term outlook.

Valuation offers another reason for his optimism, particularly following the stock's recent weakness. "At current levels, I would say that investors are worried about a doomsday scenario for Oracle, but in reality, this situation is far from bleak," the investor summed up.

Bay Area Ideas isn't the only one who thinks investors are overlooking Oracle's potential. Wall Street's numbers tell a similar story, with 27 of the 33 analysts covering ORCL recommending Buy, 5 preferring to stay on the sidelines, and just one advising Sell. That leaves Oracle with a Strong Buy consensus, while the average 12-month price target of $242.62 suggests a potential 71% upside from current levels. (See ORCL stock forecast)

data.title: Microsoft Stock (NASDAQ:MSFT) Gains After Slashing Family OneDrive Storage
data.description:
Do you take a lot of pictures? If you do, then tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) has some terrible news for you. Not be able to store nearly the number of picture files that you could previously on OneDrive. Microsoft is slashing the storage space available on OneDrive from six terabytes down to just two terabytes for its Family and Premium subscriptions. Investors seemed oddly pleased with this move, though, and gave Microsoft a more than 2% boost in Friday afternoon's trading. Microsoft has posted a 2.28% rally in its share price over the past year.

More Math From Microsoft

A report from TechPowerUp gave us the bad news; formerly subscription tiers at Microsoft 365 Family and Premium allowed one buyer to share a subscription with five other family members, with six people total using the service. Each of those users would then get one terabyte of service, which gave six terabytes for a single subscription. Microsoft then pared that back from six to two, that is, shared among the six individuals.

Microsoft is also offering additional storage capacity with OneDrive to be purchased, which will then be added to the shared pool that everyone can access. This still means that most people will be getting a whole lot less, but paying the same amount. Microsoft did not mention reasons for the cutback, though it likely has something to do with the soaring cost of storage these days.

The Xbox PC App Steps Up its Game

Meanwhile Microsoft also started rolling out the new Xbox PC app, which is set to go live by the end of the year, according to a report from Windows Central. It is not surprising to see Microsoft merge the Xbox and PC more often, because the next version of Xbox is set to run PC games as well. The new app is said to work well with both controller and keyboard/mouse combinations and users will be able to set the app as a default home screen when loading into Windows 11, which gives us some idea of how Project Helix will end up working.

One major question mark outstanding is how well the new Xbox PC app will do for discoverability when it comes to gaming. Finding new games can be difficult through Xbox, not quite as easy as it is with the Steam platform. If Microsoft can improve the Xbox's discoverability, then it may have a real competitor on its hands for Steam when Project Helix goes live and offers the best of both worlds.

data.title: Why Are Elon Musk Stocks Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) Up Today?
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) stocks were up on Friday after Elon Musk, the founder of the electric vehicle (EV) and space exploration companies, made it clear who will own the new Terafab chip factory once construction is complete. Terafab is a project under joint development by Tesla and SpaceX to establish a chip manufacturing facility in Texas.

According to Musk, Tesla and SpaceX will own the factory. That's despite the two companies getting help from semiconductor veterans Intel (INTC) and TSMC (TSM) for the construction of the plant. While Musk did say that chipmakers could lease space in the factory, it will remain firmly under the control of his only two publicly traded companies.

Investors will note that Musk's Terafab won't be just any other semiconductor manufacturing facility. Instead, Musk wants to build a 100-million-square-foot facility that would dwarf others. That plan comes with a steep price, as Musk is expected to drop a total of about $100 billion on the factory. However, he won't pay all of that at once. The initial phase of the project has a projected price tag of $10 billion to $20 billion.

Promotion

SPCX has a long & short ETF? Explore SPCM & SPCG

Why Does Musk Want Such a Large Chip Factory?

The Tesla and SpaceX CEO has a huge focus on AI and wants to develop his own chips for it. That's why he's dedicated so much to the Terafab project. While grand in scale, investors will keep in mind that this factory will serve multiple companies.

Both Tesla and SpaceX need AI for their operations. Tesla uses it for assisted driving in its EVs and it will also power the company's humanoid Optimus robots. SpaceX also takes advantage of AI for its missions, and has its own AI division named SpaceXAI, though that name is about to change to SpaceXSI. This unit of SpaceX is behind Grok, which is the AI assistant baked into X, the social media platform that Musk bought on October 27, 2022, for $44 billion. Of course, back then it was called Twitter.

TSLA and SPCX Stock Movement Today

Tesla stock rallied 2.10%, while SpaceX stock was up 1.33% on Friday. Considering the close ties between these two companies, the stocks typically rise and fall in sympathy with one another. SpaceX stock also got a boost today from its $8 billion wireless spectrum purchase.

data.title: Walmart Launches SCAN Medicare Partnership and AI Health Plans for Older Customers
data.description:
Retail giant Walmart (WMT) has launched a partnership with nonprofit insurer SCAN Health Plan to offer more personalized Medicare services to its elderly customers.

The groups have launched two co-branded Medicare Advantage plans – the SCAN Walmart Health Advantage (HMO) and SCAN Walmart Medicare Complete Chronic Special Needs Plan (C-SNP). The plans combine combine comprehensive Medicare Advantage coverage with health and wellness support designed to help older adults navigate their individual health needs with "greater support, confidence and convenience."

Two Million Medicare Enrollees

Both offerings will begin on January 1, 2027, to eligible Medicare beneficiaries in six counties in Texas and three counties in Arizona. The plans are expected to be available to more than two million Medicare enrollees.

"Walmart plays an important role in the everyday lives of many older adults, whether they're shopping for groceries, filling prescriptions or looking for products that support their health and wellness," said Zack Myers, national general manager of SCAN Health Plan. "Together, we're offering Medicare Advantage plans that combine strong benefits, personalized support and innovative tools that can help members make choices that support their individual health goals."

The companies said that they wanted to improve older adults' health and wellbeing by making it easier for members to use their benefits for things they need every day.

That includes healthy foods, as well as health and wellness products that people can buy in Walmart. In addition, there is  Walmart's Everyday Health Signals, an AI-powered platform that provides nutrition insights from everyday shopping behaviors for members who opt in. Members who choose to participate will receive tailored food recommendations based on their health goals, preferences, and shopping habits.

Value of Adult Health Plans

 "For older adults, the value of a health plan can come down to how easy it is to understand and use the benefits available to them," said Pravene Nath, M.D., group director for consumer health and data solutions at Walmart U.S. "These plans are designed to help support members and Walmart customers with the everyday decisions that impact health and wellness, from groceries and nutritious foods to prescriptions, vision, and other everyday essentials."

 C-SNP is designed for people with chronic conditions such as diabetes, congestive heart failure and cardiovascular disease.

In the U.S., Medicare Advantage plans are a private version of Medicare. It has become harder for insurers to make a profit from these plans because of rising medical care prices.

This is SCAN's second deal with a huge U.S. retailer after setting up a Medicare Advantage plan with Costco (COST).

Walmart's Health Push

For Walmart it is a further push into healthcare services. Over the next six months, it will pilot a new Health Ambassador associate role at its stores serving rural communities. Walmart said the Health Ambassadors will have "dedicated time to support customers beyond the pharmacy counter — understand their health goals and help connect them with relevant services and resources."

Back in April this year Walmart said it was expanding its care services to include weight management for the millions of Americans turning to medication to control the pounds. The company said it was expanding its Better Care Services platform with new offerings to bring together virtual care, nutrition services and pharmacy access.

That means it now includes weight management support services for customers exploring GLP-1 therapies. These are either via injections or tablets, which help stimulate weight loss.

data.title: Tesla Pivots Away From Full Self-Driving Brand in Europe—Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Gains
data.description:
Electric vehicle giant Tesla (TSLA) may have finally realized that the parenthetical disclaimers in Full Self-Driving (FSD) (Supervised) really were not helping its case. To that end, Tesla has dropped the name altogether, and has switched to Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe. It was a change investors could get behind, as Tesla stock gained almost 2.5% in Friday afternoon's trading. Tesla stock has seen a 9.31% loss in its share price over the past year.

FSD is Out the Door

A report from the LA Times described how Tesla is still trying to seek approval for full self-driving in Europe, but decided that the name might be doing more harm than good. Indeed, many circles regarded the name "Full Self-Driving" as "dangerously misleading." The United States version continues to call it "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)," but the European version has changed. This makes sense, because Tesla is trying to win favor with European regulators right now.

There is a certain logic to this move. However, the question remains whether or not this will be enough to actually sway European regulators to allow the system to be used in the first place. Given that six European nations have already approved it, the idea that it might get approval throughout the rest of the European Union really isn't out of line. But only time will tell if that turns out to be the case.

Megachargers on the Way, and in Convenient Locations

One of the biggest concerns about the Tesla Semi system is that there weren't enough chargers for it. But Tesla has been rapidly constructing Megacharger systems in order to get more electricity into their electric semi trucks. One charger station recently went into place in Georgia, and there are over a dozen more currently under construction, according to a report from InsideEVs.

The operating Tesla Megacharger is in place at a Pilot Travel Station in Ellabell, Georgia. It offers six charging stalls that can give 1.2 MW of power. The only downside to this charging station is that it doesn't allow for pull-through charging, meaning the drivers will need to back up into the bay. Pilot's vice president of alternative fuels Shannon Sturgil noted, "With these initial locations, we're making fleet electrification a more accessible option for long-haul transportation and are excited to continue working with Tesla to move at the pace and preference of our customers."

data.title: Why Is the Stock Market Up Today, 10/9/26?
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) are in the green on Friday after President Trump's vow to not strike Iran until after the November midterm elections helped ease oil prices. The two indexes are up 0.30% and 0.32%, respectively. Trump added that the U.S. and Iran are currently holding "productive discussions."

U.S. officials say negotiations have made progress, but the two sides remain divided over Iran's nuclear program. Washington wants to settle the nuclear issue before discussing other terms, while Tehran wants to address it only after reaching agreements on other matters.

Treasury Yields Climb as Oil Prices Dip

Brent crude (BZ), the global oil benchmark, is down by 0.45% to $103 per barrel. That's helped keep interest rate hike expectations low, with the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the October 28 Fed meeting currently sitting at 19.4% on the CME FedWatch tool. Lower rates benefit stocks by reducing the cost to borrow money and increasing the present value of future cash flows.
